title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: p = λn+1 is prime, a is a primitive root, and the λ-th power residues are the n elements 1, a^λ, …, a^{(n-1)λ} (proved on the previous page). This page draws consequences.

(§94, Coroll. 2) Each λ-th power residue is hit by exactly λ of the bases 1, …, λn. Hence there are many pairs (P, Q) with P^λ ≡ Q^λ but P ≢ Q (mod p). Q may be chosen freely as any nonzero class, and P = Q·r^k with r^λ ≡ 1.

(§95, Coroll. 3) If n is even, a^{nλ/2} ≡ −1 lies in the residue list. So:
- −1 is a λ-th power residue mod p = 2mλ+1.
- −1 is a λ-th power non-residue mod p = (2m+1)λ+1.
- If λ is odd, the second form cannot be an odd prime.
In modern terms, −1 = a^{λn/2} is a λ-th power iff λ divides λn/2, i.e. iff n is even.

(§96, Scholion 1, λ = 5) Primes 5n+1 (11, 31, 41, 61, 71, …) have n even, so −1 is a fifth-power residue. Hence there are P^5 ± Q^5 ≡ 0 with P ± Q ≢ 0. The cofactor is P^4 ∓ P^3Q + P^2Q^2 ∓ PQ^3 + Q^4, which equals (P² ∓ ½PQ + Q²)² − 5(½PQ)². So p divides f² − 5g² with g = PQ/2 ≢ 0, and 5 ≡ (f/g)² is a quadratic residue mod every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 5). This confirms one case of the reciprocity conjecture stated earlier in the paper.

(Next page, §97, λ = 7) The analogous identity is Φ7(P,Q) = (P³ + ½P²Q − ½PQ² − Q³)² + 7(½P²Q + ½PQ²)². It gives that −7 is a quadratic residue mod primes 7n+1.

These are exactly the cases ℓ = 5, 7 of Gauss's identity 4Φ_ℓ(x) = Y(x)² − (−1)^{(ℓ−1)/2} ℓ Z(x)² (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae §357). Euler uses them as a cyclotomic route to (ℓ*/p) = 1 for p ≡ 1 (mod ℓ).
errors: No mathematical errors. The identity (pp ∓ ½pq + qq)² − 5(½pq)² = p⁴ ∓ p³q + p²q² ∓ pq³ + q⁴ checks: the cross term gives 9/4 p²q², and subtracting 5/4 p²q² leaves p²q².
Implicit step left unstated: one needs g = pq/2 ≢ 0 mod the prime. This holds because neither P nor Q can be divisible by it (otherwise both would be, and then P ≡ Q).
Gap in scope, not an error: the method yields (5/p) = 1 only for p ≡ 1 (mod 5), not for p ≡ 4 (mod 5). So it confirms only part of the conjecture that 5 is a residue for p ≡ ±1 (mod 5).

ideas.what: -1 is a λ-th power residue mod prime λn+1 iff n is even
ideas.modern_name: power residue character of -1 in a cyclic group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler / folklore (Gauss DA for general theory)
ideas.where_published: E449 (Opuscula analytica 1, 1783); related material in E262

ideas.what: Existence of P^λ ≡ Q^λ with P ≢ Q, one of P, Q arbitrary
ideas.modern_name: kernel of the λ-th power map has order λ
ideas.where_published: E449; earlier E262 / E271-era papers on residues

ideas.what: Writing the 5th and 7th cyclotomic forms as f² − 5g² and f² + 7g², deducing that 5 resp. −7 is a quadratic residue mod primes ≡ 1 mod 5 resp. 7
ideas.modern_name: Gauss's cyclotomic identity 4Φ_ℓ = Y² − (−1)^{(ℓ−1)/2} ℓ Z² (special cases); the quadratic subfield of the cyclotomic field
ideas.where_published: E449 §§96-97 (this paper); Euler's priority for the ℓ = 5, 7 cases is noted in some histories of reciprocity (e.g. Lemmermeyer) — unsure how widely

missed.claim: Euler treats only ℓ = 5 and ℓ = 7 case by case. He does not state the general identity 4Φ_ℓ = Y² ∓ ℓZ² for prime ℓ, nor the resulting general theorem (ℓ*/p) = 1 for p ≡ 1 (mod ℓ). That is a direct precursor of Gauss §357 and of the cyclotomic proof of quadratic reciprocity. The thread was later completed by Gauss; it is not truly unexploited, though Euler's 1772 priority for these explicit decompositions is only modestly recognized.
missed.quote: qui cum sit (pp ∓ ½pq + qq)² − 5(½pq)², dabitur huiusmodi forma ff − 5gg per 5n+1 diuisibilis
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: Euler had explicit quadratic decompositions of cyclotomic polynomials about 30 years before the Disquisitiones. Mathematically it is already absorbed into standard theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The ℓ = 5 and ℓ = 7 cases of Gauss's cyclotomic identity, used to prove partial reciprocity, are a nice early anticipation. However, E449 is a known reciprocity paper discussed by historians (Weil, Lemmermeyer), so this is at most modestly under-credited.
transcription_corrections: Line 'atque adeo alterum numerorum p et q pro lubitu accipere licet' is partially obscured; 'pro lubitu' is the likely reading.
In §96, 'ita factor p ± q' reads as printed (probably intended 'ita vt factor').
The factor expression should read (pp ∓ ½pq + qq)² − 5(½pq)², which matches the image; the leading character is a smudge, not an extra symbol.
